profiles.summary: The three open questions about the Ethereum reference were closed. The reth v2.11.0-b9abbcc build that answers for Ethereum is the published v2.11.0 release, the four Nethermind 2.2.2 jump destination kernels and the erigon v3.8.1 NEON kernel give the scalar bitmap on the PoolManager runtime and about 1.1 million other inputs, and each harness reports a planted fault.

deltas.delta: Nethermind 2.2.2 picks one of four jump destination kernels by CPU and code length: Vector512 with AVX-512 VBMI for code of 64 bytes or more, Vector256 with AVX2 from 32 bytes, SSSE3 from 16 bytes, AdvSimd on arm64 from 16 bytes, and a word-at-a-time scalar scan otherwise. All four use successor-map doubling, and the Vector512 kernel adds a carry-arithmetic path for runs of PUSH1 bytes. A port to C with the same x86 instructions and a software model of the arm64 TBX and ADDP steps gives the scalar bitmap on every input tested.

profiles.summary: erigon v3.8.1 defines the read stamp of its per-frame SLOAD cache as the journal length together with a journal epoch. Every journalled state change lengthens the journal, and a revert, a reset or a finalisation moves the epoch, so a cached slot cannot outlive a write in any frame.

deltas.delta: IntraBlockState.ReadStamp is defined in execution/state/read_paths.go lines 1789-1803 as {len(journal.entries), journal.epoch}. journal.revert and journal.Reset increment the epoch (journal.go lines 115-143), and updateAccount increments it when storage is committed (intra_block_state.go line 2592). The stamp is off only when transaction IO tracing is on.

cleared.check: Lead L-1114: whether reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc, the build that gave every Ethereum reference word of the opcode comparison, is the published reth v2.11.0 release or a local modification.
cleared.result: The official v2.11.0 container image was built from commit b9abbcc1b982755baa9021e6874e2e58936ca65f with VERGEN_GIT_DESCRIBE v2.11.0 and VERGEN_GIT_DIRTY false, per its SLSA provenance. The endpoint string carries the same short commit and no modified suffix, unlike the Arbitrum One PublicNode build. The lockfile at that commit equals the tag's. The binary behind the endpoint cannot be inspected, so its identity rests on the version string, and two other Ethereum clients (geth v1.17.10 and erigon) gave the same vector answers in cycle 24.

cleared.check: Lead L-1086, Nethermind part: the four Nethermind 2.2.2 jump destination kernels (Vector512 with AVX-512 VBMI, Vector256 with AVX2, SSSE3, AdvSimd) and the word-at-a-time scalar scan against an independent scalar rule. The kernels were ported line by line to C. The three x86 kernels run the hardware instructions the .NET intrinsics name (vpermb, vpermi2b, vpshufb, pmaxsb) on a Xeon with avx512vbmi. AdvSimd is a byte-level model of TBX and ADDP. Inputs: the PoolManager runtime built from this checkout and the mainnet code (24,009 bytes, 610 destinations each), 191 prefix and 191 suffix cuts of each, 400,000 random strings in five byte mixes including long PUSH1 runs up to 1,000 bytes, every push opcode 0x5f to 0x80 at every offset in JUMPDEST fields of 1 to 200 bytes, and PUSH1 runs of every length from 1 to 200 at offsets in steps of three.
cleared.result: No mismatch and no bit set past the code length for any kernel: scalar 1,117,996 cases, Vector512 977,278, Vector256 1,065,560, SSSE3 1,096,760, AdvSimd 1,096,760 (cases below a kernel's length threshold are not dispatched to it). Planted faults are reported: a changed end offset constant gives 66,950,918 Vector512 mismatches, one changed lane bias gives 2,264,464 Vector256 mismatches, a dropped bit gives 605,953 SSSE3 mismatches, and a wrong block size gives 31,814,691 AdvSimd mismatches. Every JUMP and JUMPI target of the PoolManager is therefore accepted by every Nethermind kernel. The C port stands in for the .NET JIT output, which was not inspected.

cleared.check: Lead L-1086, erigon part: the erigon v3.8.1 NEON kernel jumpdestBitmapNEON (analysis_arm64.s) with codeBitmapNEON and markJumpdestsTail (analysis_arm64.go, analysis.go), modelled instruction by instruction with AArch64 TBL, TBX, BSL, SMAX, CMHI and UMAX semantics. The four WORD encodings were decoded field by field to SMAX V6,V0,V20, CMHI V7,V17,V6, SMAX V12,V1,V20 and CMHI V13,V17,V12, as the macro comments state. The inputs are the PoolManager runtime and mainnet code with 191 prefix and suffix cuts, 400,000 random strings and every single push in JUMPDEST fields of up to 130 bytes.
cleared.result: 690,276 cases give the scalar bitmap with no tail bits. Dropping one pointer-jumping round gives 21,063,673 mismatches and one wrong block-end byte gives 7,228, so the model detects faults. The scratch table reads stay inside the 224 zeroed bytes for every entry from 0 to 32. The model was not run on arm64 hardware.

cleared.check: Lead L-1087: the definition of erigon v3.8.1 IntraBlockState.ReadStamp and whether it changes on every journalled SetState in any frame, on every RevertToSnapshot, and on SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE2 into an address that had storage. The question is whether a stale SLOAD could serve the outer PoolManager frame after a hook reenters, as at src/PoolManager.sol:196 and 202 (checkPoolInitialized, then beforeSwap, then Pool.swap reads slot0 again) and at src/PoolManager.sol:153-159.
cleared.result: The stamp is (journal length, journal epoch) (read_paths.go lines 1789-1803). The journal only grows by append (journal.go lines 174-274), and the only truncations are revert and Reset, which both increment the epoch (lines 115-143). Every effective storage write appends a storageChange entry: stateObject.SetState (state_object.go lines 238-285), the versioned path setStateVersioned, and the fake storage used by state overrides (fakeStorageChange). A write of the value already held is skipped, which leaves the value a cached read returns unchanged. CreateAccount journals createObjectChange or resetObjectChange, Selfdestruct journals selfdestructChange, and committing storage moves the epoch (intra_block_state.go line 2592). The cache sits in each frame's CallContext and is reset when a frame starts (interpreter.go line 515). Any write by a reentered PoolManager frame, a revert of a nested frame, or a create into the address therefore changes the stamp before the outer frame reads the slot again.

leads.question: Does the .NET 10 JIT lower the Vector128 and Vector512 intrinsics of Nethermind 2.2.2 JumpDestinationAnalyzer (signed Max on sbyte without SSE4.1, unsigned LessThanOrEqual, ConditionalSelect) to the instructions the C port used, and does Vector512.IsHardwareAccelerated select the 64-byte kernel on the Intel and AMD CPUs that validators run?
leads.why: The port checked the algorithm on real AVX-512 VBMI, AVX2 and SSSE3 hardware. A JIT lowering fault on one CPU family would make that minority client reject a PoolManager JUMPDEST and fork off. It cannot move funds, so the priority is low.

leadResults.answer: For Ethereum, yes. The provenance attestation of ghcr.io/paradigmxyz/reth:v2.11.0 records VERGEN_GIT_SHA and the buildkit vcs.revision as b9abbcc1b982755baa9021e6874e2e58936ca65f, with VERGEN_GIT_DESCRIBE v2.11.0 and VERGEN_GIT_DIRTY false, and the Cargo.lock at that commit equals the tag's. The endpoint string has no modified suffix. publicnode now answers a Cloudflare challenge, and pocket serves the same reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc build. The Arbitrum One and Polygon parts belong to their units.

All four Nethermind 2.2.2 kernels and the scalar scan, ported to C with the same x86 instructions or modelled for arm64, and the erigon v3.8.1 NEON kernel, modelled instruction by instruction, give the scalar bitmap on the PoolManager runtime and mainnet code, 191 prefix and suffix cuts of each, 400,000 random strings and the single-push and PUSH1-run sets: 977,278 to 1,117,996 cases per Nethermind kernel and 690,276 for NEON, with no mismatch. Planted faults give between 7,228 and 66,950,918 mismatches. The .NET JIT lowering was not inspected, and that question is left as a low lead.

ReadStamp is defined in execution/state/read_paths.go lines 1789-1803 as the journal length and epoch. Every effective SetState in any frame appends a journal entry, RevertToSnapshot and Reset increment the epoch, CreateAccount and Selfdestruct journal their changes, and committing storage moves the epoch. A per-frame cached SLOAD therefore cannot outlive a write, a revert or a create, and the read of slot0 after a hook reenters the PoolManager sees the current word.
